A.why: Clean A-line bell from the hip in pale sky steel with a bow-wing helm; clearly a gown from above and distinct from the reference families.
A.fix: Slim the full-width block sleeves and drop the shoulder caps; carry the light colours round the dark back; add wind movement and rock-tan trim.

B.why: Bright white wind-cut skirt flares hard and reads instantly from above; winged helm.
B.fix: Slim and lighten the dark navy block sleeves that read as pauldrons; sweep the hem shards in one wind direction; add a bodice panel and a tan belt.

C.why: Stacked box tiers with no flare; reads as a squat armoured block.
C.fix: Rebuild the skirt as hip-hinged splayed panels; slim the sleeves; lighten the back.

D.why: Pretty pale robe with a plume crest, but the split panels hang straight; reads as a tabard more than a gown.
D.fix: Splay the skirt into a continuous A-line; remove the wide white cuff rings and slim the sleeves; lighten the back.

E.why: Neat light tunic; the skirt is too narrow, and the back and top-down view are dark slate.
E.fix: Hinge and widen the skirt from the hip; slim the sleeves; bring light colours to the back; turn the crate-like chest plaque into an emblem.

F.why: The wind streamer is the best zone idea on the sheet, but the ziggurat-step skirt reads as a plinth.
F.fix: Replace the stepped tiers with flared angled panels; slim the sleeves; lengthen the streamer and make it white.

notes: No candidate solved the slim sleeves: every set still uses full arm-width blocks, and that is the main shared flaw. A and B are the only real flared gowns. Most backs are dark slate and will vanish at night from the overhead camera. Rock tan is nearly absent everywhere. F's wind streamer is worth borrowing into A or B.
